images.title: 1729 is two cubes in two ways
images.purpose: Shows 1729 made as 1 cubed plus 12 cubed and also as 9 cubed plus 10 cubed.
images.composition: Plain white background, the main object large and centred with wide empty margins, no scenery, no characters, no extra decoration. One number card in the centre with one pair of cubes above it and one pair below, each joined by an arrow.
images.exact_structure: Centre: one card reading 1729, filled reddish purple (#CC79A7) with white text. Above it: one tiny cube of edge 1 and one large cube of edge 12 drawn to scale in flat oblique view, both filled teal (#0072B2), with 1³ + 12³ under them and an arrow down to the card. Below it: one cube of edge 9 and one cube of edge 10, drawn to the same scale, both filled amber (#E69F00), with 9³ + 10³ beside them and an arrow up to the card. Nothing else in the frame.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
images.takeaway: A taxicab number is a sum of two cubes in two different ways; 1729 is the smallest.
images.description: Shows 1729 made as 1 cubed plus 12 cubed and also as 9 cubed plus 10 cubed.

image_decisions.why: Two pairs of cubes meeting at one number shows the two ways of making 1729 at a glance.
